title: Find why Vercel builds hit out_of_memory at random when the Next processes peak near 2.7 GB

source.ref: Production deploy of 7426903a (#4805) ended ERROR out_of_memory on 2026-11-10 15:28Z; earlier main deploy 7d71b670 did the same.

detail: MEASURED 2026-11-10, not assumed. Of the last 30 Vercel deployments, 5 ended ERROR with out_of_memory (1 production, 4 previews). Every one died the same way: compile finished (about 93 s), then the build was killed at 'Collecting page data using 3 workers', and Vercel printed '.next/routes-manifest.json couldn't be found'. The same trees build fine on neighbouring pushes: a main deploy of the previous commit (#4806, 781c67b) and of the next ones were READY, and the HYG-215 branch OOM'd at ab52647 then built at 4896bc6. check-build-memory reads a healthy main build (2366d904) at a peak of 2770 MB summed across 4 next processes against a 7168 MB budget, so the Next processes are not near the limit. That rules out the fan-out creep the standing rule expects and points at something the sampler does not see (other processes in the container, page-data workers on a cold start, a smaller machine) or at platform noise. The failing build never prints a reading, because the sampler is killed with it. Next steps, cheapest first: (1) have the sampler write its running peak to the build log every 30 s so a killed build still leaves a number; (2) compare the Build system report (Input source code 1902 MB, node_modules 1004 MB, .git pack 337 MB) across a failing and a passing build; (3) only if the peak is real, try experimental.cpus = 2 on one preview and read the sampler. Do not raise the budget and do not cut routes until a reading says which. Production keeps serving the last READY deploy when a build fails, so this costs deploy freshness, not uptime.

verify.evidence: Close when 20 consecutive Vercel deployments (production and preview) finish READY with no out_of_memory, or when the sampler reading from a failed build names the process that grew. Read with the Vercel deployments list; the failing events carry errorCode out_of_memory.
